UPDATE 2026-09-14 — the Ampere constraint this post is built on has been LIFTED.
A community contribution (#1274,
@AntonProkopyev) makes FlashAttention accept fp8 KV on sm_86, so on two cards
ultra* no longer trades context for decode — it now has both. Everything below
was accurate when published on 2026-09-12; the sections it changed are marked and
rewritten in place. The 4- and 8-card guidance is unaffected.

Follow-up to #1024, where the fast tier benches ~100 tok/s on 2× 3090.

This part isn't one more slug — it's a naming and a shape. Every Qwen3.8-27B tier now comes in three depths of speculation, on top of two weight classes:

vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast decodes code at 220 tok/s on 2× RTX 3090 — at the full 262K context. Same two consumer cards, same 27B dense model. That is 2.2× the fast tier — from a drafter, not a bigger GPU.

⚠️ The honest qualifier, up front: that is the code-shaped prompt. (It used to cost context too — as of 2026-09-14 it no longer does on two cards; see the UPDATE above.) Narrative prose runs 123 tok/s, and the dual card now holds the full 262K while doing it. Both numbers are the canonical bench on the config as shipped. No quality number is attached yet (see the bottom).

The shape

Two weight classes — the speed series (int4) and the fidelity series (fp8) — each now in three drafter depths:

base (built-in MTP) super (DFlash2 + fp8 KV / FlashInfer) ultra (DFlash2 + fp8 KV / FlashAttn)
speed (int4) fast superfast ultrafast
fidelity (fp8) max supermax ultramax
  • super* swaps the built-in MTP head for an external DFlash2 block-drafter while keeping the base tier's fp8 KV. You keep the full context envelope; you gain code throughput; and because the drafter is external, it structurally sidesteps the built-in-MTP acceptance-collapse class entirely.
  • ultra* runs that same drafter on FlashAttention, the fastest decode path on Ampere. It used to require bf16 KV, which cost context. Since feat(qwen38): use prebuilt FlashAttention FP8 KV in ultramax #1274 it runs fp8 KV on FlashAttention, so on two cards it keeps the full envelope AND the fast path. On 4+ cards ultra* stays on bf16 KV, which already reaches 262K there (see below). fit 262K on two cards).

One drafter serves all six DFlash2 slugs. It's keyed to the base architecture, not the weight quant, so the same syvai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W4A16 drives both the int4 and the fp8 targets.

The numbers — 2× RTX 3090, TP=2, verify-full 9/9 each

Canonical bench (3 warm + 5 measured), stock vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1 + the vendored DFlash2 backport. Decode tok/s, narrative / code:

Speed series (Frozenlock AutoRound INT4)

Slug Drafter · KV / attn Ctx narr / code vs fast
dual-fast MTP n=4 · fp8 262K 73 / 100 —
dual-superfast DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 262K 78 / 141 +41% code
dual-ultrafast DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashAttn 262K 123 / 220 +120% code

Fidelity series (official Qwen FP8)

Slug Drafter · KV / attn Ctx narr / code vs max
dual-max MTP n=3 · fp8 262K 69 / 87 —
dual-supermax DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 144K 68 / 130 +49% code
dual-ultramax DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashAttn 262K 94 / 170 +95% code

All 🧪 Experimental — --force required. multi4 / multi8 variants of every tier ship too, community-validated by design (this rig has exactly two 3090s, so the first person to boot one is the validation).

Where the speed comes from — and why ultra no longer trades context

This section described a hardware wall that has since been removed. It is kept
because the mechanism still explains the tier names, and because the wall was real
until 2026-09-14. What changed is at the end of the section.

One finding drives the whole hierarchy, and it's a hardware wall worth stating plainly.

On Ampere (sm_86), stock FlashAttention and fp8 KV cache were mutually exclusive — a real kernel limit, not a config we forgot to flip. (Past tense as of 2026-09-14: a community plugin now bridges it. The original reasoning follows, because it still explains the tier names.) vLLM's FLASH_ATTN backend defers a quantized KV dtype to a capability check that requires FlashAttention 3 (Hopper) or 4 (Blackwell). Our 3090s run FA 2, which has no fp8-KV read path, so the moment you set fp8 KV, vLLM routes attention to FlashInfer instead.

That splits the DFlash2 drafter (whose block attention wants FlashAttention) two ways:

  • super* keeps fp8 KV → runs on FlashInfer → keeps the full 262K envelope, at a decode cost (~40% vs the FlashAttn path).
  • ultra* keeps FlashAttention → used to require bf16 KV → fastest decode, but bf16 KV is 2× the size, so context dropped.

⭐ What changed on 2026-09-14

@AntonProkopyev built an FA2 extension that registers fp8 KV support through the
FLASH_ATTN API on sm_86, shipped as a digest-pinned prebuilt kernel image
(#1274). Nothing compiles on
your rig. Both dual ultra slugs now run fp8 KV on FlashAttention, so the
either/or is gone on two cards:

ceiling narrative code
dual-superfast — FlashInfer 262K 82 141
dual-ultrafast — FlashAttn 262K 123 220
dual-supermax — FlashInfer 147K 70 144
dual-ultramax — FlashAttn 262K 94 170

Measured on 2× RTX 3090, bench.sh 3 warm + 5 measured. The ultrafast / superfast
pair was run at a matched ceiling so the attention backend is the only variable;
the fidelity pair ran at its shipped defaults, where the ceiling gap is itself part
of the result.

On two cards, ultra now beats super on both axes — same or more context, and
30–56% more decode. The FlashInfer path costs more than the ~40% this post
originally estimated. What that means for the super tier on duals is a separate
question and not settled here.

Two caveats worth stating: the super arms are single boots (a 50% gap cannot be
the ~1% boot-to-boot spread we measure, but don't quote the decimals), and
supermax 's code arm produced erratic token counts, so its 144 is the softest
number in the table.

So the original hierarchy wasn't arbitrary — it was the two sides of one Ampere constraint. super = "all the context, collapse-immune, faster than MTP." ultra = "maximum decode, shorter context."

Why the fidelity duals cap lower

supermax (147K) still caps below its int4 cousin. ultramax no longer does — it reached 64K only because bf16 KV was forced on it, and at fp8 it now runs the full 262K. The FP8 weights are ~29 GiB, and the external DFlash2 drafter costs ~2.6 GiB of KV pool that the built-in MTP head doesn't. On two 24 GB cards that leaves little room — bf16 KV especially. The multi4 / multi8 variants recover the full 262K once the weights split across more cards.

For 4+ GPU rigs — where the fidelity tiers stop compromising

Every tier above also ships in 4-card (multi4, TP=4) and 8-card (multi8, TP=8) form — the same speed×fidelity × base/super/ultra matrix, twelve DFlash2 slugs in all. We can't bench them (the reference rig has exactly two 3090s), so they're community-validated by design — but if you have four or more cards, this is the topology the fidelity series was waiting for.

On two cards the FP8 tiers are VRAM-starved; more cards remove the compromise. The official FP8 weights (~29 GiB) leave so little room on 2× 3090 that supermax caps at 144K and ultramax at 64K — you trade context to keep FP8 precision. Split those weights across four or eight cards and the tradeoff disappears: FP8-precision weights and the full 262K context and the DFlash2 drafter, all at once. The dual fidelity tiers are the constrained version; multi4/multi8 is where full-quality FP8 finally gets the full window. (The int4 speed tiers already fit 262K on two cards — for them, more cards buy concurrency headroom, not context.)

The DFlash2 tiers available at 4-/8-card — all 🧪 (--force), no first-party numbers (the reference rig has two cards):

Slug Series Drafter · KV / attn Context on 4+ cards
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-superfast speed (int4) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 262K
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-superfast speed (int4) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 262K
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-ultrafast speed (int4) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-ultrafast speed (int4) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-supermax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer → full 262K (dual caps at 144K)
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-supermax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer → full 262K (dual caps at 144K)
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-ultramax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K
vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-ultramax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K

The base MTP tiers ship too: vllm/qwen38-27b-{multi4,multi8}-fast and -{multi4,multi8}-max. Context on 4+ cards is a VRAM-math projection except @A1RM4X 's measured 240,635 (multi4 superfast/INT4 speed tier — see below).

There's already a strong 4-card datapoint.@A1RM4X ran the full gate on 4× RTX 3090 (#1064): verify-full 9/9, stress to 240,635 tok (91% of 256K) at 0 MiB growth, soak PASS, code decode 190 tok/s, both 8-pack arms (120/150 no-think · 128/150 think). ⚠️ That run was the INT4 speed tier on the incoai bf16 drafter (PR #1060), not the shipped syv-ai W4A16 — a strong cross-reference for the multi4-DFlash2 shape, not the exact shipped slug. The full-context-FP8 claim above follows from the VRAM math (weights split → room for 262K fp8 KV), not a first-party bench — a bench.sh on vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-supermax from any 4-card rig is what turns it from projection into a shipped row. (MTP base tier: #1025 96/119, #1004 103/135 — same 240K ceiling.)

⚠️ Budget KV headroom for DFlash2. A1RM4X's other finding: the drafter's codebooks (~0.5 GiB/GPU) + 5-layer backbone cost VRAM the KV pool wants — pushing to 512K needed --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 (0.90 OOM'd the first prefill). More cards give you the room; don't assume the MTP tier's gmu carries over.

Boot one, run report.sh --full, and file it via the numbers-from-your-rig template — that's what turns 🧪 into a shipped row.

Why the 4- and 8-card ultra slugs stay on bf16 KV

They already reach 262K on bf16, because the aggregate VRAM carries it. fp8 KV
would buy them no context and cost the same decode it costs everywhere else,
so converting them would be a regression in exchange for nothing. They are
deliberately left alone.

If you run many concurrent sequences on 4 or 8 cards there is a reason to flip
it — fp8 roughly doubles the KV pool at the same ceiling, which is headroom above
the shipped max_num_seqs: 2:

KV_CACHE_DTYPE=fp8_e4m3 bash scripts/switch.sh vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-ultrafast --force

⚠️ Untested at TP=4/8 on our side — the reference rig has two cards, and the FA2
plugin itself is validated at TP=2 only. Treat it as unproven and please report back.

Things worth knowing before you launch

⛔ No quality numbers yet. verify-full passes 9/9 on every dual slug, but the 8-pack, NIAH fill depth, and soak have not been run on any of these. Throughput without a quality number is half a picture — the c3 catalog leaves the 8pk column deliberately blank rather than imply the other half.

⚠️ Setup needs the drafter. The six DFlash2 slugs need the external drafter on disk. Fetch it with WITH_DFLASH_DRAFT=1 when you run setup.sh (it's ~1.2 GB, shared by every DFlash2 tier).

⚠️ Spec-decode is exposed to vllm#50021 — the same open GDN spec-decode index bug as the MTP tiers, still present in v0.27.1. Our collapse soak ran crash-free to 21k tokens, but treat that as "not observed," not "immune." Mitigate with SPEC_N=0.

⚠️ These decode numbers are a CUDA-13 ceiling, not a peak. Our image runs CUDA 13.0, where FlashInfer's radix top-k for the DFlash2 candidate selector can't JIT-compile and falls back to a slower sort — @oceanplexian found this in #1056. The selector's "sort-free" fast path also isn't in stock v0.27.1. So treat these figures as a floor for the config: a CUDA-12 build, or a vLLM carrying the sort-free selector path, should decode faster.

Launching these — the c3 cockpit

Every qwen3.8-27b slug — all four DFlash2 tiers × dual/multi4/multi8, plus the base MTP, single-card, and NVFP4 rows — is browsable and one-keystroke-launchable from c3, the terminal cockpit. Filter to 3.8, pick a row, press ⏎ to serve:

Install + launch (from the repo checkout):

uv pip install -e tools/serve-cockpit    # or: pip install -e tools/tui-core && pip install -e tools/serve-cockpit
c3                                        # launch  (also: python -m club3090_cockpit)

First run: press S → set your Model Dir + HuggingFace token → Ctrl+S, then r to browse the catalog. Filter to 3.8, select a slug, ⏎ serves it. c3 --lean hides the producer lane for a consumer-only view. c3 wraps the same launchers under the hood, so the DFlash2 tiers still need the external drafter on disk (WITH_DFLASH_DRAFT=1 — see "Things worth knowing" above).

Prefer the CLI? Every slug is also bash scripts/switch.sh --force <slug> — that's the form the eval commands below use.

Run the evals yourself

Same two-pass protocol as the fast-tier post (#1024) — behavioural quality (the 8-pack) + operational health. The flag-by-flag rationale (why --sampling-from-server, the two independent cli-40 timeouts, the failure-mode triage) is spelled out there and is identical here; below is the short form plus the one thing that's different: the DFlash2 slugs need the external drafter on disk — WITH_DFLASH_DRAFT=1 bash scripts/setup.sh (~1.2 GB, shared by all of them).

One-time setup — three of the eight packs build a Docker sandbox once:

pip install git+https://github.com/noonghunna/benchlocal-cli.git
git clone https://github.com/noonghunna/benchlocal-cli
bash benchlocal-cli/tools/build-sandboxes.sh     # ~30 GB free; prune if tight

⚠️ Reinstall + rebuild if you're on an older benchlocal-cli — v0.9.9 (2026-08-18) fixed the dataextract-15 / hermesagent-20 verifiers; older versions score wrong.

Quality — both reasoning legs, each its OWN boot

Instruct is the shipped default (leg A = bare launch). Going back to instruct after a thinking run needs a reboot too, or the "instruct" leg is silently a second thinking leg.

# leg A — instruct (default; no env)
bash scripts/switch.sh --force vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast
bash scripts/quality-test.sh --full --no-thinking --sampling-from-server \
  --max-tokens 4096 --thinking-max-tokens 16384 --timeout-per-case 600

# leg B — thinking  ⚠️ all FOUR sampler vars, or you run reasoning with INSTRUCT sampling
ENABLE_THINKING=true TEMP=1.0 TOP_P=0.95 PRESENCE_PENALTY=0.0 \
  bash scripts/switch.sh --force vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast
REASONING_EFFORT=low BENCHLOCAL_MODEL_TURN_TIMEOUT=900 \
bash scripts/quality-test.sh --full --enable-thinking --sampling-from-server \
  --max-tokens 4096 --thinking-max-tokens 16384 --timeout-per-case 600

Any DFlash2 slug substitutes: vllm/qwen38-27b-{dual,multi4,multi8}-{superfast,ultrafast,supermax,ultramax}.

Quality on the single-card llama.cpp slug — llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs

One 3090, TP=1, GGUF IQ4_XS, built-in MTP head, 262K context on q4_0 KV. Useful if you
have a single card, or want a second opinion on the same weights through a different engine.
Its defaults are the mirror image of the vLLM slugs above — read this before copying the
recipe.

⚠️ Thinking is the DEFAULT here, not instruct. The gate flipped 2026-09-01 on a community
request backed by #1027, where instruct
scored 120/150 pass@1 — worst of the four modes tested. So a bare launch gives you leg B,
not leg A.

Run it as shipped — full 262K, q4_0 KV, no overrides. That is what the slug is, and it is
what the numbers should describe:

# leg A — INSTRUCT.  One knob: INSTRUCT=1 flips --reasoning off AND the card's INSTRUCT
# sampler row together, so you do NOT set the four sampler vars by hand here.
FORCE=1 INSTRUCT=1 bash scripts/launch.sh --variant llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs
URL=http://localhost:8090 bash scripts/quality-test.sh --full --no-thinking \
  --sampling-from-server --max-tokens 4096 --thinking-max-tokens 16384 --timeout-per-case 600

# leg B — THINKING (the shipped default; no sampler env needed — the compose already
# ships the card's THINKING row: temp 1.0 / top_p 0.95 / top_k 20 / min_p 0.0)
FORCE=1 bash scripts/launch.sh --variant llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs
URL=http://localhost:8090 REASONING_EFFORT=low BENCHLOCAL_MODEL_TURN_TIMEOUT=900 \
bash scripts/quality-test.sh --full --enable-thinking --sampling-from-server \
  --max-tokens 4096 --thinking-max-tokens 16384 --timeout-per-case 600
  • Gated slug — and the form differs per script.launch.sh takes it as an env var (FORCE=1), switch.sh as a flag (--force). ⚠️ launch.sh … --force fails with Unknown flag: --force — this post said otherwise until 2026-09-11. The slug is hidden from switch.sh --list
    (reveal with --list --all).
  • Port is 8090, not 8020. quality-test.sh auto-detects the endpoint via preflight, but
    passing URL= explicitly avoids it finding something else you have running.
  • CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES defaults to 0, so GPU 1 stays free — you can leave a dual-card
    vLLM slug down and still run this without touching the other card.
  • --sampling-from-server on both legs: the point is to score what the compose actually
    ships, not a sampler you typed.

🔬 Bonus arm nobody has run yet: does q8 KV buy anything here?

This compose ships q4_0 KV to reach 262K on one card. Our standing rule is that sub-q8 KV
is a speed exhibit rather than serving-grade — but on this model that is a rule, not a
measurement. Nobody has the quality delta.

Re-run either leg with the q8 override and post both. It costs context (262K → 131K), which
is exactly the trade worth quantifying:

KV_TYPE=q8_0 CTX_SIZE=131072 \
  FORCE=1 bash scripts/launch.sh --variant llamacpp/qwen38-27b-single-iq4xs
# then the same quality-test.sh line as the leg above

A q4_0-vs-q8_0 pair on identical weights, sampler and packs would settle whether the KV floor
costs accuracy on Qwen3.8-27B or just headroom — please label which KV the numbers came
from, since the two are not comparable with each other or with the q8-and-above results
further up.

Operational health

bash scripts/report.sh --full     # verify + stress + soak + bench + agentic, redacted, ~43 min

Don't pair it with rebench-full.sh — same gates.

What'd help

These slugs are all 🧪 — they have throughput and no quality numbers yet, so an 8-pack on any of them is what promotes it. Most wanted:

  • A 4- or 8-card boot of the fidelity tiers (multi4-supermax / multi8-ultramax) — the full-context-FP8 claim above is VRAM math, not a bench.
  • 8-pack quality on any DFlash2 slug, either reasoning leg.
  • A CUDA-12 build — our CUDA-13 image caps the DFlash2 selector (see the note above); a CUDA-12 rig should decode faster.

Submitting is easy — and we want it even if the slugs DON'T boot on your rig:

bash scripts/report.sh --bench          # it works  -> the bench block (TPS + accept-len + peak VRAM)
bash scripts/report.sh > my-rig.md      # it doesn't -> a plain rig report (hardware + boot logs)

Drop either in a reply here or via the numbers-from-your-rig template. A rig report where a slug failed is as useful as one where it worked — a boot log + your GPU/driver/CUDA is exactly how we find the edges (CUDA-13 selector fallback, GPU-count, driver-branch mismatches).

Credits

This tier stands on community work — we used their submissions as the starting point, then shaped the slugs to our product hierarchy (a lean W4A16 drafter for more context; the speed×fidelity × base/super/ultra matrix):

  • DFlash2 is upstream vllm-project/vllm#52816; the original block-drafter checkpoint is incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2.
  • @oceanplexian (#1056) shipped the first DFlash2 dual-3090 benchmark (120/218) and the vLLM boot fixes — and flagged the CUDA-13 selector fallback above.
  • @A1RM4X (#1060) ported the 6-piece vllm#52816 overlay (the V2-speculator path that stops the checkpoint silently degrading to base DFlash) and ran the full validation gate — 8-pack, NIAH ceiling ladder to 240K, and soak — on the 4-card tier.
  • @syv-ai backported the port to v0.27.1 and requantized the drafter to W4A16 (1.2 GiB) — the lean drafter these slugs ship.

Both community PRs used the incoai bf16 drafter (11.6 GiB, which caps context at 131K); we chose the W4A16 requant to keep more of the window. We vendor all of this — we don't own it.

Pick by shape: fast / max for the full 262K on a single stream; super* for +code throughput without giving up context; ultra* when you want the fastest decode and can live inside its context window. Speed series = int4 (smaller, faster); fidelity series = official FP8 (higher-precision weights).

Upvote

One configuration-safety note that may be worth making explicit in the tier docs:

For the current Qwen3.8 DFlash2 exports, SPEC_N is coupled to the checkpoint's dflash_config.block_size; it is not a free tuning knob. The DFlash2 implementation constructs the grouped-convolution block size as 1 + num_speculative_tokens, and _grouped_conv uses that value as its causal reset boundary. The published exports declare block_size = 8, so SPEC_N=7 is the matching depth.

A mismatch can load successfully because block_size does not shape any checkpoint parameter. It instead changes the causal boundary silently and may reduce draft acceptance rather than failing at boot. In particular, SPEC_N=15 should only be paired with an export that declares block_size=16.

Suggestion: treat SPEC_N as checkpoint-coupled metadata and validate 1 + SPEC_N == dflash_config.block_size at launch, preferably failing loud on mismatch.

Follow-up: ultrafast's 231 tok/s is a short-context number — the tiers swap places by ~32K

The tables above are the canonical bench, which uses a ~25-token prompt. That's the right
protocol for comparing decode speed, and the numbers are real — but it means the hierarchy they
show (ultra > super) is measured at one end of the context range, and several of you are
running these tiers at 30K+.

We measured the same two shipped slugs across context with long one-shot prompts, spec-on as
shipped, 400 generated tokens counted from the API's own usage. The ranking inverts:

prompt ctx dual-ultrafast (bf16 / FlashAttn) dual-superfast (fp8 / FlashInfer)
~4K 124 tok/s 86 ultrafast
~8K 79 72 ultrafast
~16K 92 79 ultrafast
~32K 55 68 superfast
~90K 17 ≈72 superfast, by ~4×
~200K — (past its envelope) 66 superfast only

Spec-on decode is noisy: per-arm spread across boots is 18–37% and accept-length swings
1.84–3.41, so treat these as locating a crossover, not as precise figures. The 90K superfast
cell is a 3-boot median; the rest are single boots.

Practical routing, today, on the shipped slugs:

  • Short prompts (chat, code completion, agentic turns under ~16K) — ultrafast is the right
    pick and the 231 tok/s headline holds.
  • Long prompts (RAG over big documents, whole-repo context, long transcripts) at 32K+ —
    use superfast. It is faster and keeps the full 262K envelope. At 90K ultrafast is
    roughly 4× slower.
  • The crossover sits between 16K and 32K. If your workload straddles it, superfast is the safer
    default — it degrades gently with context where ultrafast falls off a cliff.

Why — and it isn't the KV dtype

It's the attention kernel at speculative-decode shape. Each verify step submits
num_speculative_tokens + 1 query tokens at once. FlashAttention-2's paged path forbids splitting
that work across the KV length, so it launches roughly batch × heads thread blocks and walks the
whole context serially in each — on our rig, 12 blocks on an 82-SM card. FlashInfer splits it and
keeps every SM busy.

Measured at kernel level, on identical KV bytes, q=8 versus q=1:

KV length FA2 FlashInfer
32K ×21.4 ×1.02
200K ×28.5 ×1.02

So ultrafast 's bf16-KV/FlashAttention path — the thing that makes it fastest on short prompts —
is also what makes it fall behind at depth. Same trade-off as the context envelope, just less
visible.

There is a fix, and it is upstream-pending — not shipped

Two open PRs against vLLM's FlashAttention fork lift the restriction:
vllm-project/flash-attention#176 and
#190. We arrived at the same fix
independently, found theirs first was more general, and closed ours — our tests and end-to-end
numbers are posted on both.

With that patch applied in a probe container (⚠️ not a shipped configuration, do not try to
replicate this in your compose), ultrafast at 32K goes from 55 → 111 tok/s (n=3 medians) and
retakes the lead over superfast at that depth. At 90K FlashInfer still wins, for a separate
reason the patch doesn't address.

Nothing in this section changes what you get today. The routing advice above is for the slugs
as they ship. If one of those PRs merges and reaches a vLLM release we pin, the crossover moves and
we'll update this note in one line.

Numbers: 2× RTX 3090, TP=2, vLLM v0.27.1, SPEC_N=7, thinking off, one-shot prompts,
min_tokens=400. Full method and the instrument caveats are in the probe record.

⚠️ What this means for the ultra* tiers going forward

Two things follow from the above that are worth flagging before you build around these slugs.

The advertised context on the ultra* tiers is a capability ceiling, not a usable-throughput
ceiling.dual-ultrafast declares 204,800, and the 4- and 8-card ultra* slugs declare 262,144.
The engine will boot and serve those lengths — but as the table above shows, decode past ~32K is
not something you want a workload sitting on. We are likely to cap or re-scope those advertised
numbers so the declared ceiling matches the usable range. If you have a compose pinned to a large
MAX_MODEL_LEN on an ultra* slug today, that is the change most likely to affect you, and
super* is the tier that holds long context properly.

We are not retiring the ultra* tiers. They are the fastest thing we ship at short context and
that is not an Ampere quirk — a community bench on 2× RTX 5090
(#1086 /
#1085) puts dual-ultramax at 183 tok/s
against dual-supermax at 152 on the same bench.sh instrument — the same ~20% short-context
lead, on different silicon. If you are under ~16K, ultra* remains the right pick.

Two honest limits on the above: the crossover is measured for the int4 pair (ultrafast /
superfast) on 2× 3090. For the fp8 pair (ultramax / supermax) we have no long-context

PR: #1274

Update — FA2 FP8 KV, DFlash2 and full-context vision (September 12, 2026)

I now have a working FA2 FP8-KV path on SM86 for both the FP8 target and the DFlash2 drafter, including full CUDA Graphs for draft attention. The implementation and reproducible build are published in fa2-fp8kv-sm86.

These measurements use vLLM 0.27.1, pinned to vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1@sha256:0a51ea5b4ae2dc5d81890e5173f54203d2a3ae0cfffe51b8fd2afd4391bfd967. Current club-3090 master has moved to 0.29.0; The completed 0.29.0 validation is in the HYPERMAX update above. The numbers below are not 0.29.0 results.

The configuration keeps official FP8 target weights, DFlash2 W4A16 n=7, FP8 E4M3 KV for both models, 262,144 context, one sequence, and vision up to about 4 MP. PCIe P2P is enabled through NCCL; custom all-reduce is disabled in this run. That differs from the September 8 P2P update below.

The custom decoder attention uses FA2. GDN and the vision encoder keep their normal implementations. The FLASHINFER registry enum is retained for its cache-layout contract, but the custom target/draft path does not execute FlashInfer attention kernels. For long prefill, FP8 KV is unpacked once per bounded block into temporary BF16 workspace and processed by native FA2, with FP32 merging. Persistent KV remains FP8. The prefill improvement comes from this path and removing the extra 1,024-token prefill cap; DFlash2 stays at n=7.

Original P2P-off report (historical baseline)

Measured a locally tuned supermax configuration on September 8. The target remains official Qwen3.8-27B-FP8; only the external drafter is W4A16.

Logs, runtime versions, launch settings, and the additional local overlays: public gist.

Hardware / configuration Value

The fixed KV pool reported 267,493 cache tokens. Automatic sizing either left too little KV for 262K or overestimated the available pool and failed allocation in earlier attempts. Decode used three warmups and five measured runs per prompt, with the standard 1,000-token narrative and 800-token code caps. Thinking was disabled. Temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, and min_p 0.0 were all sent explicitly.
Prefill used fresh haystacks and client-observed input-token/TTFT rates. The benchmark called vLLM directly, without LiteLLM.

Operational checks and limits

  • verify-full.sh: PASS, nine applicable checks; unused Genesis check skipped. Text, tools, streaming tool calls, reasoning, and vision passed.
  • Vision fixture: 4/4. A separate 2048×2048 PNG also scored 4/4, with 4,131 input tokens and a 17-token response in 4.44 s.
  • Context control strings succeeded at 9,846, 29,347, 173,583, and 260,289 actual input tokens.
  • At 173,583 tokens, prefill was 845.7 tokens/s, taking 205.256 s. At 260,289 it was 707.8 tokens/s, taking 367.740 s.
  • Stress used STRESS_FAST=1: the separate 60K/90K stress rungs were skipped, and the ceiling ladder had two rungs. The 90K benchmark was separate.
  • Stress still failed its margin gate: 449 MB free VRAM < 1,024 MB. The threshold was not relaxed.
  • Observed per-card peaks through the sampled benchmark period, stress, and 4 MP vision test: 23,978 / 23,976 MiB. The separate per-card sampler started after narrative measurement 2; the benchmark's full-run aggregate peak was 47,354 MiB.
  • Benchmark post-run memory was 126 MiB above idle in aggregate. There was no soak, so this is not a zero-growth or leak-free claim.

The 260K text test and the 4 MP image test were separate requests. Uniform-haystack checks establish addressability, not document-retrieval quality. The 68/130 decode figures are for short prompts, not sustained generation at 260K.

The runtime also had the local final-DFlash2-sampling-contract and MRV2-thinking-budget overlays; the gist includes them and the exact base revision. No full quality packs, continuous soak, or extended agentic ramp were run for this configuration. I would keep it experimental with this VRAM margin.

Skip to content UPDATE 2026-09-14 — the Ampere constraint this post is built on has been LIFTED. A community contribution (#1274, @AntonProkopyev) makes FlashAttention accept fp8 KV on sm_86, so on two cards ultra* no longer trades context for decode — it now has both. Everything below was accurate when published on 2026-09-12; the sections it changed are marked and rewritten in place. The 4- and 8-card guidance is unaffected.Follow-up to #1024, where the fast tier benches ~100 tok/s on 2× 3090.This part isn't one more slug — it's a naming and a shape. Every Qwen3.8-27B tier now comes in three depths of speculation, on top of two weight classes:vllm/qwen38-27b-dual-ultrafast decodes code at 220 tok/s on 2× RTX 3090 — at the full 262K context. Same two consumer cards, same 27B dense model. That is 2.2× the fast tier — from a drafter, not a bigger GPU.⚠️ The honest qualifier, up front: that is the code-shaped prompt. (It used to cost context too — as of 2026-09-14 it no longer does on two cards; see the UPDATE above.) Narrative prose runs 123 tok/s, and the dual card now holds the full 262K while doing it. Both numbers are the canonical bench on the config as shipped. No quality number is attached yet (see the bottom). The shape Two weight classes — the speed series (int4) and the fidelity series (fp8) — each now in three drafter depths: base (built-in MTP) super (DFlash2 + fp8 KV / FlashInfer) ultra (DFlash2 + fp8 KV / FlashAttn) speed (int4) fast superfast ultrafast fidelity (fp8) max supermax ultramax super* swaps the built-in MTP head for an external DFlash2 block-drafter while keeping the base tier's fp8 KV. You keep the full context envelope; you gain code throughput; and because the drafter is external, it structurally sidesteps the built-in-MTP acceptance-collapse class entirely.ultra* runs that same drafter on FlashAttention, the fastest decode path on Ampere. It used to require bf16 KV, which cost context. Since feat(qwen38): use prebuilt FlashAttention FP8 KV in ultramax #1274 it runs fp8 KV on FlashAttention, so on two cards it keeps the full envelope AND the fast path. On 4+ cards ultra* stays on bf16 KV, which already reaches 262K there (see below). fit 262K on two cards).One drafter serves all six DFlash2 slugs. It's keyed to the base architecture, not the weight quant, so the same syvai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W4A16 drives both the int4 and the fp8 targets. The numbers — 2× RTX 3090, TP=2, verify-full 9/9 each Canonical bench (3 warm + 5 measured), stock vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.1 + the vendored DFlash2 backport. Decode tok/s, narrative / code:Speed series (Frozenlock AutoRound INT4) Slug Drafter · KV / attn Ctx narr / code vs fast dual-fast MTP n=4 · fp8 262K 73 / 100 — dual-superfast DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 262K 78 / 141 +41% code dual-ultrafast DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashAttn 262K 123 / 220 +120% code Fidelity series (official Qwen FP8) Slug Drafter · KV / attn Ctx narr / code vs max dual-max MTP n=3 · fp8 262K 69 / 87 — dual-supermax DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 144K 68 / 130 +49% code dual-ultramax DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashAttn 262K 94 / 170 +95% code All 🧪 Experimental — --force required. multi4 / multi8 variants of every tier ship too, community-validated by design (this rig has exactly two 3090s, so the first person to boot one is the validation). Where the speed comes from — and why ultra no longer trades context This section described a hardware wall that has since been removed. It is kept because the mechanism still explains the tier names, and because the wall was real until 2026-09-14. What changed is at the end of the section.One finding drives the whole hierarchy, and it's a hardware wall worth stating plainly.On Ampere (sm_86), stock FlashAttention and fp8 KV cache were mutually exclusive — a real kernel limit, not a config we forgot to flip. (Past tense as of 2026-09-14: a community plugin now bridges it. The original reasoning follows, because it still explains the tier names.) vLLM's FLASH_ATTN backend defers a quantized KV dtype to a capability check that requires FlashAttention 3 (Hopper) or 4 (Blackwell). Our 3090s run FA 2, which has no fp8-KV read path, so the moment you set fp8 KV, vLLM routes attention to FlashInfer instead.That splits the DFlash2 drafter (whose block attention wants FlashAttention) two ways:super* keeps fp8 KV → runs on FlashInfer → keeps the full 262K envelope, at a decode cost (~40% vs the FlashAttn path).ultra* keeps FlashAttention → used to require bf16 KV → fastest decode, but bf16 KV is 2× the size, so context dropped.⭐ What changed on 2026-09-14 @AntonProkopyev built an FA2 extension that registers fp8 KV support through the FLASH_ATTN API on sm_86, shipped as a digest-pinned prebuilt kernel image (#1274). Nothing compiles on your rig. Both dual ultra slugs now run fp8 KV on FlashAttention, so the either/or is gone on two cards: ceiling narrative code dual-superfast — FlashInfer 262K 82 141 dual-ultrafast — FlashAttn 262K 123 220 dual-supermax — FlashInfer 147K 70 144 dual-ultramax — FlashAttn 262K 94 170 Measured on 2× RTX 3090, bench.sh 3 warm + 5 measured. The ultrafast / superfast pair was run at a matched ceiling so the attention backend is the only variable; the fidelity pair ran at its shipped defaults, where the ceiling gap is itself part of the result.On two cards, ultra now beats super on both axes — same or more context, and 30–56% more decode. The FlashInfer path costs more than the ~40% this post originally estimated. What that means for the super tier on duals is a separate question and not settled here.Two caveats worth stating: the super arms are single boots (a 50% gap cannot be the ~1% boot-to-boot spread we measure, but don't quote the decimals), and supermax 's code arm produced erratic token counts, so its 144 is the softest number in the table.So the original hierarchy wasn't arbitrary — it was the two sides of one Ampere constraint. super = "all the context, collapse-immune, faster than MTP." ultra = "maximum decode, shorter context." Why the fidelity duals cap lower supermax (147K) still caps below its int4 cousin. ultramax no longer does — it reached 64K only because bf16 KV was forced on it, and at fp8 it now runs the full 262K. The FP8 weights are ~29 GiB, and the external DFlash2 drafter costs ~2.6 GiB of KV pool that the built-in MTP head doesn't. On two 24 GB cards that leaves little room — bf16 KV especially. The multi4 / multi8 variants recover the full 262K once the weights split across more cards. For 4+ GPU rigs — where the fidelity tiers stop compromising Every tier above also ships in 4-card (multi4, TP=4) and 8-card (multi8, TP=8) form — the same speed×fidelity × base/super/ultra matrix, twelve DFlash2 slugs in all. We can't bench them (the reference rig has exactly two 3090s), so they're community-validated by design — but if you have four or more cards, this is the topology the fidelity series was waiting for.On two cards the FP8 tiers are VRAM-starved; more cards remove the compromise. The official FP8 weights (~29 GiB) leave so little room on 2× 3090 that supermax caps at 144K and ultramax at 64K — you trade context to keep FP8 precision. Split those weights across four or eight cards and the tradeoff disappears: FP8-precision weights and the full 262K context and the DFlash2 drafter, all at once. The dual fidelity tiers are the constrained version; multi4/multi8 is where full-quality FP8 finally gets the full window. (The int4 speed tiers already fit 262K on two cards — for them, more cards buy concurrency headroom, not context.) The DFlash2 tiers available at 4-/8-card — all 🧪 (--force), no first-party numbers (the reference rig has two cards):Slug Series Drafter · KV / attn Context on 4+ cards vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-superfast speed (int4) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 262K vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-superfast speed (int4) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer 262K vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-ultrafast speed (int4) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-ultrafast speed (int4) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-supermax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer → full 262K (dual caps at 144K) vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-supermax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · fp8 / FlashInfer → full 262K (dual caps at 144K) vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-ultramax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K vllm/qwen38-27b-multi8-ultramax fidelity (fp8) DFlash2 · bf16 / FlashAttn 262K The base MTP tiers ship too: vllm/qwen38-27b-{multi4,multi8}-fast and -{multi4,multi8}-max. The full-context-FP8 claim above follows from the VRAM math (weights split → room for 262K fp8 KV), not a first-party bench — a bench.sh on vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-supermax from any 4-card rig is what turns it from projection into a shipped row. (MTP base tier: #1025 96/119, #1004 103/135 — same 240K ceiling.) ⚠️ Budget KV headroom for DFlash2. A1RM4X's other finding: the drafter's codebooks (~0.5 GiB/GPU) + 5-layer backbone cost VRAM the KV pool wants — pushing to 512K needed --gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 (0.90 OOM'd the first prefill). More cards give you the room; don't assume the MTP tier's gmu carries over.Boot one, run report.sh --full, and file it via the numbers-from-your-rig template — that's what turns 🧪 into a shipped row. Why the 4- and 8-card ultra slugs stay on bf16 KV They already reach 262K on bf16, because the aggregate VRAM carries it. fp8 KV would buy them no context and cost the same decode it costs everywhere else, so converting them would be a regression in exchange for nothing. They are deliberately left alone.If you run many concurrent sequences on 4 or 8 cards there is a reason to flip it — fp8 roughly doubles the KV pool at the same ceiling, which is headroom above the shipped max_num_seqs: 2:KV_CACHE_DTYPE=fp8_e4m3 bash scripts/switch.sh vllm/qwen38-27b-multi4-ultrafast --force ⚠️ Untested at TP=4/8 on our side — the reference rig has two cards, and the FA2 plugin itself is validated at TP=2 only. Treat it as unproven and please report back. Things worth knowing before you launch ⛔ No quality numbers yet. verify-full passes 9/9 on every dual slug, but the 8-pack, NIAH fill depth, and soak have not been run on any of these. Throughput without a quality number is half a picture — the c3 catalog leaves the 8pk column deliberately blank rather than imply the other half.⚠️ Setup needs the drafter. The six DFlash2 slugs need the external drafter on disk. Fetch it with WITH_DFLASH_DRAFT=1 when you run setup.sh (it's ~1.2 GB, shared by every DFlash2 tier).⚠️ Spec-decode is exposed to vllm#50021 — the same open GDN spec-decode index bug as the MTP tiers, still present in v0.27.1. Our collapse soak ran crash-free to 21k tokens, but treat that as "not observed," not "immune." Mitigate with SPEC_N=0.⚠️ These decode numbers are a CUDA-13 ceiling, not a peak. Our image runs CUDA 13.0, where FlashInfer's radix top-k for the DFlash2 candidate selector can't JIT-compile and falls back to a slower sort — @oceanplexian found this in #1056. The selector's "sort-free" fast path also isn't in stock v0.27.1. So treat these figures as a floor for the config: a CUDA-12 build, or a vLLM carrying the sort-free selector path, should decode faster.
